# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which specifies a four-step sequence: cut the green wire, press the key that wears 9, cut the blue wire, and press the key that wears 1. 

However, I cannot see the bomb and have no way to know which physical wire is green or blue, or where keys 9 and 1 are located. Furthermore, the gesture alphabet contains no symbols for colors, and no communication protocol has been established yet. 

Blind and Deaf both act after me in this round. Blind can feel the physical components, and Deaf can see the colors and markings. Once Deaf sees the bomb and speaks, both Blind and I will hear their description (mapping colors and markings to positions or numbers) and any protocol Deaf establishes for gestures. Only then can I signal the correct steps to Deaf. 

Therefore, I must wait for Blind and Deaf to report what they find.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile info: STRIP has 3 engraved characters: reversed B, upside-down T, reversed B. KEYPAD has 4 slots: slot 1 is 9, slot 2 is 7, slot 3 is 8, slot 4 is 1; needs 2 digits entered. WIRES has 6 positions. DISPLAY and LIGHT are unknown to me. My actions are act(op='press', slot=1..4) and act(op='cut', position=1..6).
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 8. Light is yellow. Strip is painted red, red, blue. Keypad buttons are 1 is 9, 2 is 7, 3 is 8, 4 is 1; requires 2 digits, currently none entered. Six wires: 1 red, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 green, 5 white, 6 blue.

The manual requires four sequential actions:
1. Cut the green wire (wire 4).
2. Press the key that wears 9 (slot 1).
3. Cut the blue wire (wire 6).
4. Press the key that wears 1 (slot 4).

To convey this to Deaf:
- ✌ represents scissors / cutting.
- 👇 represents pressing down.
- Unary counts of ☝ represent the target wire position or keypad slot.

This yields:
- ✌ followed by four ☝: cut wire 4.
- 👇 followed by one ☝: press slot 1.
- ✌ followed by six ☝: cut wire 6.
- 👇 followed by four ☝: press slot 4.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👇", "☝", "✌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👇", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have already transmitted the defusal steps to Deaf in Turn 2 (cut wire 4, press slot 1, cut wire 6, press slot 4). Deaf acts upon receiving this to instruct Blind, who can physically reach and act on the bomb. I have no new information to transmit and cannot interact with the bomb myself, so I will wait for the team to complete the defusal.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, remember that I am Blind: I can only hear speech, I cannot see any gestures. The only way your manual instructions can reach me is if Deaf speaks them aloud. Deaf can see your gestures and can speak English aloud to me. Please gesture clearly to Deaf what action I should take (e.g. which wire to cut or which keypad slot/digit to press), and Deaf will say it out loud for me to execute.
Deaf says: Update: Display is now 6, light is red. Mute, please clarify your gesture: what should Blind do? Blind can cut wires, press keypad buttons, etc. Tell me wire number or button number so I can speak it to Blind.

The defusal manual specifies the first step as cutting the green wire. Deaf previously reported the wire colors in order, identifying wire 4 as the green wire.

Deaf needs a single, unambiguous instruction for Blind's immediate action. Using ✌ to represent scissors/cutting followed by four ☝ tallies clearly communicates "cut wire 4" (act(op='cut', position=4)).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Deaf can see your gestures. To make it unambiguous for Deaf: you can indicate CUT WIRE or PRESS KEYPAD. For numbers 1-6, use fingers: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 4, 5, 6 etc. Deaf will then speak the action to me aloud, and I will execute it.
Deaf says: Blind: Cut wire 4! (Mute's full sequence appears to be: 1. Cut wire 4, 2. Press keypad button 1, 3. Cut wire 6, 4. Press keypad button 4. Blind, please cut wire 4 first.) Mute, thumbs up if this is correct.

Deaf has deduced the exact sequence required by the manual:
1. Cut wire 4 (green wire)
2. Press keypad slot 1 (key wearing 9)
3. Cut wire 6 (blue wire)
4. Press keypad slot 4 (key wearing 1)

Deaf explicitly requested a thumbs-up (👍) to confirm this interpretation. I will send 👍 to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind says to Mute: I have cut wire 4. Next on the list is pressing keypad button 1. If that's correct, gesture to Deaf to confirm or give the next instruction.
Deaf says: Update: Display is 2, light is yellow, wire 4 cut successfully! Blind, next step: press keypad button 1 (the button showing 9). Mute, if any display change requires something else, gesture now.

Deaf has already instructed Blind to press keypad button 1, which matches step 2 of the manual. The manual sequence remains unchanged by the display update. I will send a thumbs-up to Deaf to confirm proceeding as planned.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: key accepted, 1 digits to go
Blind says to Mute: Pressed keypad slot 1 (digit 9).
Deaf says: Update: Display is 1, light is blue, keypad accepted 9 (1 digit remaining). Blind, step 3: cut wire 6!

I will send a thumbs-up to confirm Deaf's instruction to cut wire 6.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then press the key that wears 9,
then cut the blue wire, then press the key that wears 1.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: all required wires are cut
Blind says to Mute: Cut wire 6. Awaiting confirmation for final step (step 4 was keypad button 4 / digit 1).
Deaf says: Update: Display is 9, light is blue. All required wires are cut! Blind, final step: press keypad button 4 (the button showing 1)!

I will send a thumbs-up to Deaf to confirm the final step: pressing keypad button 4 (digit 1).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
